title: Training, CPR certification and competency required to administer under the circular
rule_summary: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124 provides that, to administer, a pharmacist or pharmacy intern must first receive training that is accredited by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the American Council on Pharmaceutical Education or a similar health authority or professional body appropriate for the medications being administered and their respective patient populations, and such training shall include learning modules on techniques for administration by injection. To administer, a pharmacist or pharmacy intern must maintain current certification in cardiopulmonary resuscitation; must maintain continued competency regarding the populations served, medications administered and current guidelines, continuing education programs being one way to maintain competency; and must maintain competency in management of medical emergencies that may arise as a result of administration of eligible medications. Prescribers are urged to issue separate prescriptions for appropriate emergency medications, as needed.
exam_relevance: Tests the qualifications a pharmacist or intern must hold before and while administering under the circular, that the training must be accredited and include injection-technique modules, and that continuing education is one way, not the only way, to maintain competency.

authority.name: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Pharmacist Administration of Medications, March 11, 2026
authority.section: Training; CPR Certification; Continued Competency; Administration – Medical Emergencies, first and third sentences

common_confusions: Treating any injection training as sufficient, when the circular requires training accredited by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the American Council on Pharmaceutical Education or a similar health authority or professional body appropriate for the medications and patient populations, including injection-technique modules.
Treating CPR certification as a one-time step rather than a certification that must be kept current.
Treating continuing education as the only way to maintain competency.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-14 in Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Pharmacist Administration of Medications, dated March 11, 2026, in the Word document linked from the Department's news page on mass.gov.
